messages:
erin: Noticed weirdness: toggling the 'exclude retries' button in the latency pane made p95 jump ~40ms for /api/v1/query. Anyone else?
jon: I saw that too. p50 barely moved. p95 and p99 increased and dashboard showed sample_count went down but percentile moved the wrong direction. Feels like a merge artifact.
li: Which endpoint variant and time window? Could be tdigest vs raw sample mismatch.
nera: It was Endpoint Breakdown -> 30m -> endpoint=/api/v1/query -> aggregation=tdigest (rollup). I compared against the raw samples query in observability and the numbers diverged.
ci-bot: ci: metric-collector deployed rollup merger v2 at 2026-03-21T17:02Z to canary clusters.
jon: Hypothesis: UI applies tag filters client-side after fetching a merged tdigest that already incorporated retry-tagged samples, then recomputes percentiles using the merged histogram's counts incorrectly.
li: If the library subtracts counts from a merged tdigest you get nonsense. tdigest subtraction is not valid. Are we doing subtraction anywhere?
nera: The console is currently calling /metrics/rollup?range=30m&endpoint=/api/v1/query and then applying exclude_retries=true client-side as a filter. So yes, client subtracts.
jon: Repro steps I ran: 1) query raw samples include_retries=true -> N=2,400 p95~210ms 2) raw exclude_retries -> N=1,900 p95~185ms 3) dashboard (rollup then client filter) -> shows p95~225ms even though sample_count=1900 in UI.
li: That exactly matches tdigest-subtraction artifact. Fix options: a) server supports filtered rollups so UI can request rollup computed on exact filters, b) UI switches to fetching raw sample percentiles when filters are non-trivial, c) disallow client-side filter toggle for rollup widgets.
nera: I'd prefer (a) because rollups keep bandwidth and compute cheap for big time windows. We should extend /metrics/rollup to accept tag filters including retry=true/false and forward to rollup builder. Also return explicit sample_count and an attribution field like "rollup_computed_with_filters": "retry=false".
jon: +1. Also add an explicit badge in the widget header that says "percentile source: rollup (filters applied)" or "raw samples". Users keep getting surprised.
li: I'll open a small API PR to accept query params and plumb them through the rollup joiner. We'll also add warnings when requested filter cannot be satisfied with existing rollup shards (fallback to raw).
nera: QA: after API change let's run a diff job: for top 100 endpoints, compute p95(raw exclude_retries) vs p95(rollup exclude_retries) over last 24h and surface any >5% disagreement. Put results in a dashboard so SRE/product can monitor.
ci-bot: ci: created job metrics-audit/rollup-filter-diff to run nightly.
jon: Good. Timeline: Li PR by EOD, canary tomorrow onto console-integrations, then opt-in audit. Erin can you file INF-4120 to track?
erin: Filed INF-4120 "rollup-filter-consistency: add server rollup filtering + UI attribution" assigned to eng-platform. I'll also add a UI ticket to prevent the toggle from misleading users until the server side is ready.
qa-bot: qa: test plan added to ticket INF-4120: include unit test for query param passthrough, e2e that compares rollup vs raw for one hour window.
jon: Thanks all. Short-term mitigations: disable client-side subtraction on rollup widgets and show a tooltip "filter not applied to computed percentile; request server-side filtered rollup" until PR ships.
nera: I'll coordinate the tooltip copy with UX.
li: I'll post the PR link when ready.
erin: Closing loop: we should also document in the console docs a short note about which filters are supported by rollups and how percentiles are computed. Saves support noise.
